records.source: שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ שִׁ֥ירוּ לַ֝יהוָ֗ה כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Sing to YHWH a new song; sing to YHWH, all the earth.
pieces: Sing a new song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q All the earth, sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

L.1: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a new song; \q sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the earth.

R.1: Sing a new song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Everyone on earth, sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

decisions.reason: Most of this psalm (verses 1b-13a) appears, with small differences, in 1 Chronicles 16:23-33, in the song sung when David brought the ark of God to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a new song: fresh praise for what God has done
decisions.reason: A new song answers a new act of God (33:3; 40:4; 98:1). Isaiah 42:10 calls the ends of the earth to sing one.

decisions.choice: all the earth: everyone on earth
decisions.reason: The whole earth is called on, that is, all its peoples (verses 3, 7, 10), not Israel only.

records.heading: A new song for all the earth

records.source: שִׁ֣ירוּ לַ֭יהוָה בָּרֲכ֣וּ שְׁמ֑וֹ בַּשְּׂר֥וּ מִיּֽוֹם־לְ֝י֗וֹם יְשׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Sing to YHWH, bless his name; bear news from day to day [of] his salvation.
pieces: Raise your song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \q Day after day announce the good news of how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves.

L.2: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; \q bear news from day to day of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} salvation.

R.2: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! \q Tell the good news every day: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves!

decisions.choice: bless his name: praise God, speak well of him
decisions.reason: To bless (barak) God is to praise him and give him honor; "his name" is God himself as he has made himself known.
The verb (basar) is to bring news, usually good news, as in Isaiah 40:9 and 52:7.
Readable says what blessing God's name means (m1).

records.gloss: Recount among the nations his glory, among all the peoples his wonders.
pieces: Tell the nations of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, \q and all the peoples of the wonders {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

L.3: Recount among the nations {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, \q among all the peoples {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders.

R.3: Tell the other nations how great and glorious {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is. \q Tell people everywhere about the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

decisions.reason: The word (kavod) is literally weight, and so the greatness and splendor of God that deserves honor.
The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's great acts, such as the rescue from Egypt (Exodus 3:20; 78:4).

records.source: כִּ֥י גָ֘ד֤וֹל יְהוָ֣ה וּמְהֻלָּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד נוֹרָ֥א ה֝֗וּא עַל־כָּל־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: For great [is] YHWH and to be praised exceedingly; to be feared [is] he above all gods.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is great and worthy of the highest praise; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must be revered above every god.

L.4: For great [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and greatly to be praised; \q to be feared [is] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} above all gods.

R.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserves all our praise. \q People should honor and fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} far more than any so-called god.

decisions.choice: to be feared: to be held in awe
decisions.reason: The form (nora') means one who is to be feared, that is, honored with awe and reverence (47:3).
As in 95:3, the other gods are not real rivals; verse 5 says what they are.
Readable prepares for verse 5, which says these gods are nothing (m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י׀כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָעַמִּ֣ים אֱלִילִ֑ים וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם עָשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: For all [the] gods of the peoples [are] worthless idols, but YHWH made [the] heavens.
pieces: For every god the peoples serve is a mere nothing, an idol, \q but it was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who made the heavens.

L.5: For all the gods of the peoples [are] worthless idols, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the heavens.

R.5: The gods of the other nations are only idols. They are nothing! \q But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the sky above us.

decisions.reason: The word ('elilim) means worthless things and is used for idols. It sounds like the word for gods ('elohim), a play on words: the gods of the peoples are no-gods (Isaiah 2:8; Leviticus 19:4).

decisions.choice: made the heavens: the Creator above the gods
decisions.reason: The nations' gods were made by people; the LORD made the sky, where the nations placed their gods. That is the proof of who is God (115:3-4).

records.gloss: Splendor and majesty [are] before him; strength and beauty [are] in his sanctuary.
pieces: Splendor and majesty stand in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence; \q strength and beauty fill {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place.

L.6: Splendor and majesty [are] before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q strength and beauty [are] in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sanctuary.

R.6: Glory and royal greatness surround {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q Power and beauty fill the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives.

decisions.choice: splendor and majesty: the glory of a king
decisions.reason: The pair (hod, hadar) is used of a king's splendor (21:6; 45:4). Here they stand before the LORD like attendants at his throne.
The parallel in 1 Chronicles 16:27 reads "strength and joy are in his place"; there the ark had not yet a temple.
Readable says what the sanctuary is: God's holy house.

records.source: הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת עַמִּ֑ים הָב֥וּ לַ֝יהוָ֗ה כָּב֥וֹד וָעֹֽז׃
records.gloss: Ascribe to YHWH, clans of [the] peoples, ascribe to YHWH glory and strength.
pieces: Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what is due, you families of the nations; \q give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} glory and might.

L.7: Ascribe to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, families of the peoples, \q ascribe to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} glory and strength.

R.7: Give honor to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you families and nations! \q Say that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is glorious and strong.

decisions.reason: The verb (yahav) is simply "give"; giving glory and strength to God is acknowledging that they are his.
Verses 7-9 echo 29:1-2, where the same call is made to the heavenly beings; here it goes out to the families of all the peoples (Genesis 12:3).

records.source: הָב֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה כְּב֣וֹד שְׁמ֑וֹ שְׂאֽוּ־מִ֝נְחָ֗ה וּבֹ֥אוּ לְחַצְרוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Ascribe to YHWH [the] glory of his name; lift up an offering and come into his courts.
pieces: Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the glory {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name deserves; \q bring a gift and enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} courts.

L.8: Ascribe to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; \q lift up an offering and come into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} courts.

R.8: Honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name deserves. \q Bring a gift to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and come into the courtyards of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple.

decisions.choice: an offering: a gift or tribute
decisions.reason: The word (minchah) is a gift, the tribute brought to a king (2 Samuel 8:2), and the grain offering of the temple (Leviticus 2:1). The nations come like subjects to their King.

decisions.choice: his courts: the courtyards of the temple
decisions.reason: Worshipers gathered in the open courts around the temple building.
Readable says whose courts these are.

records.source: הִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה בְּהַדְרַת־קֹ֑דֶשׁ חִ֥ילוּ מִ֝פָּנָ֗יו כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Bow down to YHWH in [the] adornment of holiness; tremble before him, all the earth.
pieces: Bow low before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in holy splendor; \q tremble in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence, all the earth.

L.9: Bow down to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in [the] splendor of holiness; \q tremble before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, all the earth.

R.9: Bow down and worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who is holy and glorious. \q Everyone on earth, tremble before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!

decisions.choice: the splendor of holiness: God's holy splendor
decisions.reason: The phrase (hadrat qodesh) may describe God's holy splendor, the setting of the worship, or the holy attire of those who worship (as in 29:2; 2 Chronicles 20:21). Literal keeps it open; Readable takes it of God.
The verb (chil) is to writhe or tremble, here in awe before the King.
Readable takes the phrase of God himself (m1).

records.source: אִמְר֤וּ בַגּוֹיִ֨ם׀יְה֘וָ֤ה מָלָ֗ךְ אַף־תִּכּ֣וֹן תֵּ֭בֵל בַּל־תִּמּ֑וֹט יָדִ֥ין עַ֝מִּ֗ים בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Say among the nations, 'YHWH reigns! Yes, [the] world is established; it will not be shaken. He will judge [the] peoples with uprightness.'
pieces: Tell the nations, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is King! \q The world stands firm; nothing can make it totter. \q He will judge the peoples fairly."

L.10: Say among the nations, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} reigns! \q Indeed, the world is established; it will not be shaken. \q He will judge the peoples with uprightness."

R.10: Tell all the nations, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is King! \q He has made the world firm, so it cannot be shaken. \q He will judge all people fairly."

decisions.choice: reigns: is King, has taken the throne
decisions.reason: The verb (malak) with the LORD as subject is the cry of Psalms 93, 96, 97 and 99. The same form was shouted when a new king took the throne (2 Samuel 15:10; 2 Kings 9:13), so it may also mean "has become King": the LORD is acclaimed as King over all the earth.
"The world is established; it will not be shaken" repeats 93:1. Because the LORD is King, the world he made holds firm.
The verb (din) is to judge or govern; "uprightness" (mesharim) is what is level and fair. The King's judging means setting things right.
Balanced and Readable say "is King", the plain sense of the royal cry; Literal keeps "reigns".
Readable names who made the world firm, which the passive verb implies.

records.source: יִשְׂמְח֣וּ הַ֭שָּׁמַיִם וְתָגֵ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ יִֽרְעַ֥ם הַ֝יָּ֗ם וּמְלֹאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad; let the sea thunder and its fullness.
pieces: Let the heavens be full of joy and the earth be glad; \q let the sea thunder with all that lives in it.

L.11: Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad; \q let the sea thunder, and its fullness.

R.11: Let the sky and the earth be happy! \q Let the sea and all the creatures in it roar!

decisions.choice: its fullness: all that fills the sea
decisions.reason: The word (melo') is what fills something; here the creatures of the sea (24:1).
The sea is often a picture of chaos and threat (93:3-4); here even the sea thunders in praise of its King. Psalm 98:7 repeats the line.

records.source: יַעֲלֹ֣ז שָׂ֭דַי וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֑וֹ אָ֥ז יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ כָּל־עֲצֵי־יָֽעַר׃
records.gloss: Let [the] field exult and all that [is] in it; then all [the] trees of [the] forest will shout for joy
pieces: Let the fields and everything in them celebrate; \q then every tree in the woods will cry out with joy,

L.12: Let the field exult and all that [is] in it; \q then all the trees of the forest will shout for joy,

R.12: Let the fields and everything in them be glad. \q Then all the trees in the forest will sing for joy.

decisions.choice: the trees shout for joy: creation welcomes its King
decisions.reason: The poem pictures the whole creation, sky, sea, fields and forest, celebrating the King's coming, as in Isaiah 55:12.
"Then" points to the moment named in verse 13, when the LORD comes to judge.
"Before the LORD" in verse 13 completes this line, so the verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָ֨ה׀כִּ֬י בָ֗א כִּ֥י בָא֮ לִשְׁפֹּ֪ט הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ יִשְׁפֹּֽט־תֵּבֵ֥ל בְּצֶ֑דֶק וְ֝עַמִּ֗ים בֶּאֱמוּנָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: before YHWH, for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge [the] world with righteousness and [the] peoples with his faithfulness.
pieces: in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is on the way, on the way to judge the earth. \q He will bring justice to the world \q and judge its peoples by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own faithfulness.

L.13: before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to judge the earth. \q He will judge the world with righteousness \q and the peoples with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithfulness.

R.13: They will sing in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is coming. He is coming to rule the earth as judge. \q He will judge the world with justice \q and treat all peoples with faithfulness.

decisions.choice: judge: rule and set things right
decisions.reason: The verb (shafat) means more than passing sentence: it is to govern and to put wrongs right. For a world under wrong, the coming of this Judge is good news, and creation sings.

decisions.choice: for he comes, for he comes: repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: The repetition makes the arrival urgent and near. The form can mean "he has come" or "he is coming"; the joy of verses 11-12 looks forward to it.
Psalm 98:9 ends with almost the same words; the parallel in 1 Chronicles 16:33 stops after "to judge the earth".
Readable ended verse 12 with a full stop, so it repeats the subject: the trees sing before the LORD.
